campaignMasters.title: Window study
campaignMasters.prompt: IMK3GIK. Use image 1 as the PRIMARY reference for the exact 2008 Mark III helmet, shoulder construction and real photographed surface character. Preserve the fine warm-gold metallic texture, subtle tonal variation, tight gold faceplate cuts, red helmet frame, narrow white eye slits, painted shoulder surfaces and visible collar mechanics from image 1. Use image 2 only as a SECONDARY construction reference for the same suit, especially the upper chest and circular reactor; do not copy its smoother material finish. Make a modest new camera angle approximately 30 degrees off frontal, a calm three-quarter view rather than a profile. Widen the framing to show the COMPLETE helmet with breathing room above, both shoulder assemblies and upper chest down to the circular reactor. Hands and lower body stay outside the frame. One figure only. Preserve intact, clean, carefully maintained armor with the fine existing surface texture, without adding battle grime, dirt, scorched metal or heavy scratches. Crisp lens focus on helmet and chest, fine surface detail, natural highlight rolloff and restrained exposure; no soft-focus treatment or motion blur. A credible live-action film frame, not a glossy showroom presentation. The figure stands just inside a quiet industrial room beside a large cool north-facing window. Broad soft blue-gray daylight wraps gently around the helmet and shoulder, with a small neutral interior bounce preserving the warmth of the gold alloy. Pale window frames and simple concrete architecture remain legible in the background. Place the helmet slightly left of center in the wide frame. The same natural gold and red surface response as image 1, uneven fine reflections rather than polished chrome; balanced cool surroundings and warm metal, open shadows, no theatrical rim light. Keep the scene clear and still, without fog or a blurred wash of light.

campaignMasters.title: Repulsor systems check
campaignMasters.prompt: Both images depict the same single armored figure. Image 1 defines the airport scene, full body, pose and precise red and gold panel layout. Image 2 defines the helmet, shoulders and chest only. Locked camera, full body visible, continuous six-second shot. The figure stands completely grounded with both feet planted throughout, arms relaxed slightly away from the hips. First two seconds: thrusters off, unchanged original armor. Seconds two to three: a brief low-power ignition from the centers of the palms and the undersides of the boot soles only, a small downward white-blue exhaust. At second three the exhaust switches off completely. Final three seconds: hold still with thrusters fully off and the armor looking exactly as it did before ignition. The eyes and circular chest reactor retain their original steady white light throughout. All red and gold armor plates, thighs, shins and panel seams are opaque, non-emissive metal. Only brief soft reflected light from the exhaust is permitted on these surfaces; it disappears immediately when the exhaust stops. No added luminous strips, hot metal, glowing seams, scorched marks or altered panel colors. Preserve armor geometry. No lift-off, no walking, no camera movement, no cuts, no text. Audio: brief soft mechanical ignition and shutdown against quiet rain, no dialogue or music.
campaignMasters.reviewNotes: Grounded ignition and shutdown study. Reflected light clears in inspected post-shutdown frames; not a guarantee of takeoff fidelity.

campaignMasters.title: Controlled ascent
campaignMasters.prompt: A single continuous six-second cinematic shot. The armored figure in the supplied first frame activates its palm and boot repulsors and lifts smoothly off the wet airport apron into a low, controlled hover. Its legs remain extended and its hands angle slightly outward to stabilize the ascent. Concentrated white-blue thrust sends small ripples and a restrained spray across the puddles beneath its boots. The camera tilts upward gently to retain the full figure. Preserve the supplied armor construction, closed helmet, circular chest reactor, proportions and red-and-gold materials throughout. Cool overcast lighting remains consistent. No cuts, armor transformation, new weapons, text or graphics. Audio: a controlled rising repulsor hum with gentle rain, no dialogue or music.

sampleResults.title: Stratosphere
sampleResults.prompt: IMK3GIK Mark III armor in powered flight high above a vast sunlit cloud ocean at dawn. Dynamic three-quarter frontal view, one armored fist leading toward camera, full body readable in a diagonal composition, distant curved cloud horizon, tiny boot thruster plumes. Golden sunlight skims burgundy-red plates and gold faceplate against cold blue sky. Photographed as a practical cinematic miniature, precise mechanical seams, realistic metal, circular white chest reactor, restrained eye light, no luminous armor seams. Wide 16:9 cinematic key art, no text or logos.

sampleResults.title: After the landing
sampleResults.prompt: IMK3GIK Mark III armor in a controlled three-point landing on a black volcanic plain. Low wide camera close to ground, one gauntlet planted, opposite knee raised, helmet tilted toward viewer, anatomically coherent armored limbs. Fine ash lifts in a shallow ring, no explosion. A distant low sun silhouettes jagged mountains and warm dust while a cool sky reflects on red metallic plates and gold helmet. Circular chest arc reactor, authentic Mark III panel relationships. Cinematic practical-effects photography with clear silhouette and sharp armor. No text, logos or glowing leg stripes.

sampleResults.title: Harajuku landing
sampleResults.prompt: One continuous six-second cinematic shot of Iron Man Mark III descending into an iconic three-point landing in Harajuku, Tokyo at night, then settling into stillness. Keep the same core action as the reviewed landing pass, but place him on a wet urban street with distinctive Harajuku energy: modern storefront glow, layered Japanese street signage, crosswalk markings, reflected neon color in puddles, and dense city atmosphere kept slightly soft behind the subject so the armor remains dominant and readable. Begin just before impact with restrained downward velocity, then land cleanly: one fist to the ground, one knee bent, opposite arm swept back, a controlled burst of mist, street spray, and light debris pushed outward. After impact, hold for a brief heroic settle with subtle head and shoulder stabilization and fading boot/palm exhaust. Preserve exact Mark III armor construction and panel relationships above all else: red and gold metallic armor, closed gold faceplate, narrow illuminated eye slits, circular chest reactor, accurate helmet proportions, chest geometry, shoulders, gauntlets, thighs, shins, and boots. Emission only from boot soles and palm centers during descent/impact; chest reactor and eyes stay at normal steady brightness. Armor surfaces remain non-emissive metal with realistic reflections from Tokyo signage. No suit transformation, no extra glowing seams, no invented armor details, no cuts, no text or logos in the image, no camera shake, no scorched damage.

trainingDatasets.name: Mark III - Motion Training Set
trainingDatasets.notes: Interview case-study sources, not studio-authorized production assets. Video source is a user-selected enhanced YouTube upload; its 8K label does not establish native detail. Existing source overlay and thin borders are retained. Training clips are center-trimmed to 22 or 39 frames at 24 fps, with no optical-flow interpolation or audio. Three adjacent dodge/fire/walk-away clips are reserved and never uploaded for training. This is a sequence holdout within the same film and setting, not an independent pretraining-contamination test. Nine stills supplement detail and pose coverage; near-duplicate film frames were omitted. No generated media are training targets. H3 hosted license coverage remains unverified; user instructed proceeding on 2026-09-08.
